subject: Quarterly commit reconciliation & smoothing-credit proposal
content:
From: Anna Morales <anna@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on commit reconciliation cadence and credits

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo today. Procurement and finance had a couple of follow-ups specifically about how Redwood handles usage vs commit reconciliation:
- Does Redwood do quarterly or annual reconciliation by default?
- If we underuse a quarterly commit, do you invoice the shortfall immediately or do you offer credits?
- Any examples you can share for smoothing short-term volatility?

I've attached our projected usage sheet. Can you share the process we should expect if we sign a 12-month commit?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Morales
Director of Platform Procurement
Acme Analytics
Attachment: Acme_Commit_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

-----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on commit reconciliation cadence and credits

Hi Anna — great question. Summary up front: Redwood supports both quarterly and annual reconciliation; our standard for hosted usage-based commits is quarterly reconciliation with an optional smoothing-credit mechanism for early volatility. Details below.

Quick bullets (high level):
- Commit tiers and pricing: per-token rates are tiered by committed monthly token volume. See attached Redwood_Recon_Process_v1.pdf for the rate table.
- Reconciliation cadence: default = quarterly (end of each fiscal quarter we compare committed vs actual token consumption). Annual reconciliation is available if preferred (single reconciliation at year end + monthly reporting).
- Shortfalls: by default, shortfalls are invoiced at the contracted per-token rate at reconciliation.
- Smoothing-credit: as a customer-friendly option, we can offer an initial smoothing buffer where the first quarter shortfall up to 15% is converted to an account credit (not invoiced) and carried forward; subsequent shortfalls are invoiced.
- Make-goods (one-off true-ups): for customers who prefer not to be invoiced mid-year, we can structure an annual true-up with a cap (e.g., max 25% of committed volume converted to credits across the year).

I attached an examples workbook (Smoothing-Credit-Examples.xlsx) with three scenarios (steady growth, front-loaded spike, and under-utilization). Let me know which cadence you prefer and I can circulate a formal term sheet.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Recon_Process_v1.pdf (PDF)

-----
From: Ben Carter <ben@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Anna Morales <anna@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on commit reconciliation cadence and credits

Thanks Sean. Two quick clarifications from finance:
1) If we pick quarterly with smoothing-credit (15% first-quarter buffer), does Redwood deduct that credit from the next invoice automatically, or is it a separate line item?
2) For annual true-up option, will Redwood require an additional prepayment reserve at contract start?

—Ben

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@acmeanalytics.com>, Anna Morales <anna@acmeanalytics.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on commit reconciliation cadence and credits

Hi Ben — quick answers:
1) Smoothing-credit is applied as an invoice credit line item on the next monthly invoice after reconciliation. It shows as "Smoothing credit (Q2 shortfall)" and reduces the payable amount; we can also show it as a separate credit memo if your AP team prefers.
2) Annual true-up: we do not require an additional reserve by default, but larger enterprise deals sometimes include a small upfront deposit (1-2% of annual commit) that becomes a credit against the final reconciliation to simplify cash flow. If you want that route we can add it to the term sheet.

I'll loop in billing to confirm invoice formatting.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Anna Morales <anna@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on commit reconciliation cadence and credits

Sean / Marissa — procurement prefers the annual true-up (single reconciliation) to keep accounting simpler, but finance is worried about year-end surprises. Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide quarterly usage reports (no billing) so we can self-monitor?
2) If we do an annual true-up, can we get a cap on the annual make-good invoiced amount (e.g., max 20% of annual commit) and a phased bill (bill half at reconciliation, half 30 days later)?

If you can confirm those, we can move to a redline review.

Best,
Anna

-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna@acmeanalytics.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on commit reconciliation cadence and credits

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks. We can accommodate both items with the following commercial guardrails: 

1) Quarterly visibility: Redwood will provide read-only monthly usage exports to your finance team (S3 link or CSV) with token-level breakdowns and rolling forecasts. These are purely informational if you select annual reconciliation.

2) Annual true-up with capped exposure: we will agree to an annual make-good cap of 20% of the annual committed tokens. Billing cadence for the make-good can be split: 50% invoiced at reconciliation, 50% invoiced 30 days later. The standard contracted per-token rates apply to any billed shortfall.

3) Small protection for early churn: if a customer reduces committed volume by >30% within the first 90 days, we treat that as a termination adjustment and apply a pro-rated credit for unused prepayments (if any).

4) Legal/contract language: we'll add a short clause to the SOW that defines "Reconciliation" (annual vs quarterly), the "Make-Good Cap" percentage, and the "Smoothing Credit" mechanics (only applicable if quarterly reconciliation is chosen).

I asked Priyom to draft the amendment language and Marissa to confirm billing treatment. Sean — please send Acme the term sheet reflecting this and attach the example workbook.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Smoothing-Credit-Examples.xlsx (spreadsheet)

-----

Thread notes: internal coordination followed by external confirmation. Attachments include pricing worksheets and a short recon-process PDF. The thread documents a common pattern of negotiation: customer asks for lower risk on volatility; Redwood offers visibility + configurable reconciliation cadence + capped annual exposure.
